title: Wendelin: proper object — Christ for me and special mercy applied by faith
source_text: XXIV. Quibus consona docet Wendelinus Christianae Theologiae lib. 2. cap. 24. ubi haec est ejus undecima Thesis: Proprium, principale, & proximum objectum Fidei est promissio Evangelica de peccatis per & propter Christi mortem expiatis, omnibusque peccatoribus poenitentibus & credentibus, propter Christum crucifixum fide apprehensum, in gratiam ex misericordia receptis; hanc promissionem in specie singuli fideles per fidem sibi applicant, & sic ad salutem dicuntur credere. Quibus hanc subjungit explicationem, Fidei justificantis objectum proprium est Christus pro nobis, me, te, crucifixus, & gratuita remissio peccatorum propter Christi mortem, & fusum pro nobis sanguinem, singulis per fidem applicanda; quae alias appellatur specialis misericordia.
pass_a_gloss: With which Wendelin teaches in agreement in Christian Theology book 2, chapter 24, where this is his eleventh Thesis: The proper, principal, and proximate object of Faith is the Evangelical promise concerning sins expiated through and for the sake of Christ's death, and concerning all penitent and believing sinners received into grace from mercy for the sake of Christ crucified apprehended by faith; this promise each of the faithful applies to himself by faith in particular, and thus they are said to believe unto salvation. To which he subjoins this explanation: The proper object of justifying faith is Christ crucified for us, for me, for you, and the free remission of sins for Christ's death and blood poured out for us, to be applied to each by faith; which otherwise is called special mercy.
pass_b_english: Wendelin (Chr. Theol. II.24, th. 11): proper/principal/proximate object = Evangelical promise of sins expiated by Christ’s death.
Penitent believers received into grace for Christ crucified apprehended by faith.
Each applies that promise to himself in particular — thus believes unto salvation.
Explanation: Christ crucified for us/me/you + free remission by His blood — special mercy applied by faith.
